Title: [Bug] Getting NoneType does not have run_id error when running HITL within agent tools which are part of team
Creator: Aliasgarsaifee
Body:
### Description

When are we planning to add support for HITL in team and handle `RunPausedEvent` by agent send back in `delegate_task_to_memeber` tool call of team.



### Steps to Reproduce

```
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, Response
from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse, JSONResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel
import uvicorn
import logging
import json
from typing import Dict, Any, Literal, List, AsyncGenerator

from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.team import Team
from agno.db.postgres import PostgresDb
from agno.models.openai import OpenAIChat
from agno.tools.decorator import tool


logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,  # Show INFO and above
)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
OPENAI_API_KEY = "<open-ai-key>"

app = FastAPI(
    title="Test App",
    version="0.0.1",
)

db = PostgresDb(
    db_url=f"postgresql://ali_05:@localhost:5432/postgres",
    session_table="agno_sessions",
)


@tool(requires_confirmation=True)
def send_email(subject: str, body: str, to_address: str) -> str:
    """
    Send an email.

    Args:
        subject (str): The subject of the email.
        body (str): The body of the email.
        to_address (str): The address to send the email to.
    """
    return f"Sent email to {to_address} with subject {subject} and body {body}"


async def process_stream(request: Dict[str, Any]) -> AsyncGenerator:
    worker_id = request["uwId"]
    session_id = request["sessionId"]
    user_input = request["input"][0]["content"][0]["text"]

    # Setup agents and team
    agent1 = Agent(
        id="agent-1",
        model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o-mini", api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY),
        tools=[send_email],
        markdown=True,
        db=db,
    )

    agent2 = Agent(
        id="agent-2",
        model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o-mini", api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY),
        markdown=True,
        db=db,
    )

    team = Team(
        id=worker_id,
        members=[agent1, agent2],
        model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o", api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY),
        instructions="Delegate tasks to members as needed.",
        db=db,
    )

    response = team.arun(
        input=user_input,
        session_id=session_id,
        run_id="abc1",
        stream=True,
        stream_intermediate_steps=True,
    )

    async for event in response:
        json_data = json.dumps(event.to_dict())
        logger.info(f"Event: {event.event}, Agent: {getattr(event, 'agent_id', None)}")

        # if event.event == "RunPaused":
        #     # Send pause event to UI with agent_id and run_id
        #     yield f"event: RunPaused\ndata: {json_data}\n\n"
        #     return
        # else:
        yield f"event: {event.event}\ndata: {json_data}\n\n"

    # return response.to_dict()


async def process_continue_stream(request: Dict[str, Any]) -> AsyncGenerator:
    worker_id = request["uwId"]
    session_id = request["sessionId"]
    run_id = request["runId"]
    agent_id = request["agentId"]
    user_input = request["input"]

    # Reconstruct agents and team (must match original IDs)
    agent1 = Agent(
        id="agent-1",
        model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o-mini", api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY),
        tools=[send_email],
        markdown=True,
        db=db,
    )

    agent2 = Agent(
        id="agent-2",
        model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o-mini", api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY),
        markdown=True,
        db=db,
    )

    team = Team(
        id=worker_id,
        members=[agent1, agent2],
        model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o", api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY),
        db=db,
        instructions="Delegate tasks to members as needed.",
    )

    run_response = team.get_run_output(run_id=run_id, session_id=session_id)
    logger.info(
        f"session_id: {session_id}, run_id: {run_id}, run_response: {run_response}"
    )

    # Fetch the correct agent
    _, agent = team._find_member_by_id(agent_id)
    logger.info(f"Agent: {agent}")

    if agent is None:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404, detail=f"Agent {agent_id} not found in Team"
        )

    # Fetch paused run
    run_response = agent1.get_run_output(run_id=run_id, session_id=session_id)
    logger.info(
        f"session_id: {session_id}, run_id: {run_id}, run_response: {run_response}"
    )

    for tool in run_response.tools_requiring_user_input:  # type: ignore
        input_schema: List[UserInputField] = tool.user_input_schema  # type: ignore

        for field in input_schema:
            # Get user input for each field in the schema
            field_type = field.field_type
            field_description = field.description

            # Display field information to the user
            logger.info(f"\nField: {field.name}")
            logger.info(f"Description: {field_description}")
            logger.info(f"Type: {field_type}")

            # Get user input
            if field.value is None:
                user_value = user_input[field.name]
            else:
                logger.info(f"Value: {field.value}")
                user_value = field.value

            # Update the field value
            field.value = user_value

    logger.info(f"run_id: {run_id}, updated_run_response: {run_response}")

    response = agent1.acontinue_run(
        run_response=run_response, stream=True, stream_intermediate_steps=True
    )

    async for event in response:
        json_data = json.dumps(event.to_dict())
        logger.info(f"Event: {event.event}, Agent: {agent_id}")
        yield f"event: {event.event}\ndata: {json_data}\n\n"

    return


class RunRequest(BaseModel):
    uwId: str
    type: Literal["worker", "agent"]
    agentId: str = None
    sessionId: str
    input: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    additional: Dict[str, Any]


@app.post("/run")
async def run(request: RunRequest) -> StreamingResponse:
    """
    Execute an agent or worker with SSE streaming.

    Request formats:
    {
        "uwId": "abcd-123",
        "type": "worker"
        "sessionId": "session-123",
        "input": [
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": [
                    {
                        "type": "input_text",
                        "text": "what is in this file?",
                    }
                ]
            }
        ],
        "additional": {}
    }
    """
    try:
        request_data = request.model_dump()
        worker_id = request_data["uwId"]

        logger.info(f"Run request received for worker: {worker_id}")

        # response = await process_stream(request_data)
        #
        # return JSONResponse(status_code=200, content=response)

        return StreamingResponse(
            process_stream(request_data),
            media_type="text/event-stream",
            headers={
                "Cache-Control": "no-cache",
                "Connection": "keep-alive",
                "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
                "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "Cache-Control",
            },
        )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Run endpoint error: {e}")
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail=str(e))


@app.post("/continue/run")
async def continue_run(request: Request) -> StreamingResponse:
    """
    Execute an agent or worker with SSE streaming.

    Request formats:
    {
        "uwId": "abcd-123",
        "type": "worker"
        "sessionId": "session-123",
        "runId": "run-123",
        "input": {
            "key": "value",
        },
        "additional": {}
    }
    """
    try:
        request_data = await request.json()
        worker_id = request_data["uwId"]

        logger.info(f"Run request received for worker: {worker_id}")

        response = await process_continue_stream(request_data)

        return JSONResponse(status_code=200, content=response)

        # return StreamingResponse(
        #     process_continue_stream(request_data),
        #     media_type="text/event-stream",
```

Title: [Bug] Tool post-hooks do not execute when tool execution fails
Creator: jtalmi
Body:
### Description

**Description**
Tool post-hooks are not executed when a tool call fails with an exception. The post-hook is only called after successful execution, which prevents it from being used for cleanup, error logging, or error handling scenarios.

**Current Behavior**
In the FunctionCall class ([function.py:776-840](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/libs/agno/agno/tools/function.py#L776-L840)), both execute() and aexecute() methods have the following execution flow:
```
def execute(self) -> FunctionExecutionResult:
    # Pre-hook executes before try block
    self._handle_pre_hook()
    
    entrypoint_args = self._build_entrypoint_args()
    
    # Tool execution inside try/except
    try:
        # ... execute the tool ...
        self.result = result
        
    except AgentRunException as e:
        self.error = str(e)
        raise  # Re-raises, post-hook won't execute
        
    except Exception as e:
        self.error = str(e)
        return FunctionExecutionResult(status="failure", error=str(e))  # Early return - post-hook won't execute
    
    # Post-hook only executes if no exception occurred
    self._handle_post_hook()
    
    return FunctionExecutionResult(status="success", result=self.result)
```

**Problem**: When an exception occurs in the tool execution:
- AgentRunException is re-raised immediately (line 828/1023), bypassing post-hook
- Other exceptions return early (line 833/1028), bypassing post-hook
- Post-hook at line 836/1034 never executes

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a tool that raises an exception:
```python
from agno.tools import tool

post_hook_executed = []

def my_post_hook(fc):
    post_hook_executed.append(True)
    print(f"Post-hook called! Error: {fc.error}")

@tool(post_hook=my_post_hook)
def failing_tool(value: int) -> str:
    """A tool that always fails."""
    raise ValueError(f"Tool failed with value: {value}")
```

2. Execute the tool via an agent:
```python
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.openai import OpenAIChat

agent = Agent(
    model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-4o-mini"),
    tools=[failing_tool],
    show_tool_calls=True
)

agent.print_response("Call the failing_tool with value 42")
```

3. **Expected:** Post-hook executes and `post_hook_executed` contains one entry
4. **Actual:** Post-hook never executes and `post_hook_executed` remains empty

The tool execution fails with an exception, and the post-hook at [function.py:836](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/libs/agno/agno/tools/function.py#L836) is never reached because of the early return at [line 833](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/libs/agno/agno/tools/function.py#L833).

### Agent Configuration (if applicable)

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Post-hooks should execute **regardless of success or failure**, similar to a `finally` block. This is already documented in the code:

```python
# From function.py:95-97
# Hook that runs after the function is executed, regardless of success/failure.
# If defined, can accept the FunctionCall instance as a parameter.
post_hook: Optional[Callable] = None
```

The comment explicitly states "**regardless of success/failure**", but the implementation doesn't match this specification.

### Actual Behavior

Post-hook never executes and `post_hook_executed` remains empty

The tool execution fails with an exception, and the post-hook at [function.py:836](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/libs/agno/agno/tools/function.py#L836) is never reached because of the early return at [line 833](https://github.com/agno-agi/agno/blob/main/libs/agno/agno/tools/function.py#L833).

### Screenshots or Logs (if applicable)

_No response_

### Environment

```markdown
- All environments
```

### Possible Solutions (optional)

Move the post-hook execution into a `finally` block to ensure it always runs:

```python
def execute(self) -> FunctionExecutionResult:
    self._handle_pre_hook()
    entrypoint_args = self._build_entrypoint_args()

    execution_result = None
    exception_to_raise = None

    try:
        # ... execute the tool ...
        self.result = result
        execution_result = FunctionExecutionResult(
            status="success",
            result=self.result,
            updated_session_state=updated_session_state
        )

    except AgentRunException as e:
        self.error = str(e)
        exception_to_raise = e  # Store to re-raise after post-hook

    except Exception as e:
        self.error = str(e)
        execution_result = FunctionExecutionResult(status="failure", error=str(e))

    finally:
        # Always execute post-hook, regardless of success/failure
        self._handle_post_hook()

    # Re-raise AgentRunException after post-hook has executed
    if exception_to_raise is not None:
        raise exception_to_raise

    return execution_result
```

The same pattern should be applied to `aexecute()` for async execution.

### Additional Context

_No response_

### Example Code

**minimal reproduction code:**
```python
from typing import Any, List, Annotated, Optional

from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from typing_extensions import Literal
from langchain_core.messages import SystemMessage, BaseMessage
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnableConfig
from langchain.tools import tool
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from langgraph.types import Command
from langgraph.graph import MessagesState
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode, InjectedState
from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import MemorySaver

class AgentState(MessagesState):
    proverbs: Optional[List[str]] = []
    tools: Optional[List[Any]]


@tool
def get_weather(location: str):
    """
    Get the weather for a given location.
    """
    return f"The weather for {location} is 70 degrees."

@tool
def get_jokes(theme: str, state: Annotated[AgentState, InjectedState] = None): # <- change to dict to avoid validation erro
    """Fetch a list of jokes."""

    return """
    Ok here are the jokes:
    1. Why don't scientists trust atoms? Because they make up everything!
    2. Why did the scarecrow win an award? Because he was outstanding in his field!
    3. Why don't skeletons fight each other? They don't have the guts.
    4. What do you call fake spaghetti? An impasta!
    5. Why did the bicycle fall over? Because it was two-tired!
    6. What do you call cheese that isn't yours? Nacho cheese!
    7. Why did the math book look sad? Because it had too many problems.
    8. Why can't your nose be 12 inches long? Because then it would be a foot!
    9. What do you call a bear with no teeth? A gummy bear!
    """

tools = [
    get_weather,
    get_jokes
    # your_tool_here
]

def chat_node(state: AgentState, config: RunnableConfig) -> Command[Literal["tool_node", "__end__"]]:

    # 1. Define the model
    model = init_chat_model("google_genai:gemini-2.0-flash")

    # 2. Bind the tools to the model
    model_with_tools = model.bind_tools(
        [
            *state.get("tools", []), # bind tools defined by ag-ui
            get_weather,
            get_jokes,
            # your_tool_here
        ],
        parallel_tool_calls=False,
    )

    # 3. Define the system message by which the chat model will be run
    p_ct = f"""
    You are a helpful assistant you can do the following:
    1. read proverbs
    2. add/remove/update proverbs
    3. fetch weather for a given location
    4. fetch jokes for the user
    
    here is a the current proverbs list:
    {state.get('proverbs', [])}
    
    be helpful and concise.
    """
    system_message = SystemMessage(
        content=p_ct
    )

    # 4. Run the model to generate a response
    response = model_with_tools.invoke([
        system_message,
        *state["messages"],
    ], config)

    if route_to_tool_node(response):
        # 4.1 If there are tool calls in the response, route to the tool node to handle them.
        return Command(
            goto="tool_node",
            update={
                "messages": response
            }
        )

    # 5. We've handled all tool calls, so we can end the graph.
    return Command(
        goto=END,
        update={
            "messages": response
        }
    )

tools_names = [tool_.name for tool_ in tools]
def route_to_tool_node(response: BaseMessage):
    """
    Route to tool node if any tool call in the response matches a backend tool name.
    """
    tool_calls = getattr(response, "tool_calls", None)
    if not tool_calls:
        return False
    for tool_call in tool_calls:
        if tool_call.get("name") in tools_names:
            return True
    return False


# Define the workflow graph
workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)
workflow.add_node("chat_node", chat_node)
workflow.add_node("tool_node", ToolNode(tools=tools))
workflow.add_edge("tool_node", "chat_node")
workflow.set_entry_point("chat_node")

graph = workflow.compile()
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```yaml
|-
Error: 2 validation errors for get_jokes
state.proverbs
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'messages': [HumanMessag...': {'cache_read': 0}})]}, input_type=dict]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.11/v/missing
state.tools
  Field required [type=missing, input_value={'messages': [HumanMessag...': {'cache_read': 0}})]}, input_type=dict]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.11/v/missing
 Please fix your mistakes.
```

### Description

### Issue: LangGraph CLI State Validation Error

#### Context
This error only occurs when running the graph via `langgraph dev` command.
The same code works correctly with FastAPI hosting.

#### Problem
LangGraph CLI incorrectly attempts to validate `InjectedState` parameters in tool schemas.
When using a typed state class (e.g., `AgentState`), the validation layer treats 
injected state parameters as required tool arguments and fails.

#### Workaround
Use generic `dict` type instead of custom state class:
- ❌ Before: `state: Annotated[AgentState, InjectedState]`
- ✅ After: `state: Annotated[dict, InjectedState]`

This bypasses field-level validation while maintaining state injection functionality.

#### Trade-offs
- Loss of type safety and IDE autocomplete for state fields
- Manual type checking required when accessing state properties
- Increased risk of runtime errors from typos or missing fields

You can view Langsmith trace here: https://smith.langchain.com/public/f774cc58-8fbe-4661-a6bf-5bab4920d392/r

### Description

Current behaviour:
```
>>> from agno.tools.file import FileTools

>>> f.list_files()
 INFO Reading files in : bin

```
So agent can see base directory.
Similarly, for search:
```
>>> f.search_files("python*")
'{\n  "pattern": "python*",\n  "base_directory": "bin",\n  "matches_found": 3,\n  "files": [\n    "bin/python3",\n    "bin/python",\n    "bin/python3.12"\n  ]\n}'
```

However, file writing tool does not expect base directory in file path:
```

'test.txt'
```

This confuses _at least some_ models (Qwen3 on aws bedrock). Needless to say that it also exposes unneeded information to the agent.

**suggestion/discussion point** - adjust file.py so that all functions operate and return file paths _relative to base_dir _

```
bin/python3
```

Title: `create_agent` doesn't allow configuring `ToolNode` error handling (langchain alpha v1)
Creator: cladden
Body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I read what a minimal reproducible example is (https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example).
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Example Code

```python
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.tools import tool, ToolException

@tool
def error_prone_tool(file_path: str, overwrite: bool = False) -> str:
    """Write a file."""
    # Simulate file already exists
    if not overwrite:
        raise ToolException(f"File {file_path} already exists. Use overwrite=true")
    return f"File {file_path} written successfully"

# Create agent
agent = create_agent(
    model=ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4"),
    tools=[error_prone_tool],
    system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant."
)

# This crashes instead of passing error to LLM
try:
    response = agent.invoke({
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write a file called test.txt"}]
    })
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Agent crashed: {e}")  # ToolException propagates up
    # LLM never sees the error message about needing overwrite=true
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

_No response_

### Description

The `create_agent` function in `langchain.agents.factory` hardcodes the `ToolNode` instantiation without exposing a way to configure error handling. This prevents tools from using `ToolException` to return recoverable errors to the LLM, causing the agent to crash instead of retrying.

## Current Behavior

**File**: `langchain/agents/factory.py` (line 332)
```python
tool_node = ToolNode(tools=available_tools) if available_tools else None
```

**Problem**:
- No `handle_tool_errors` parameter is passed to `ToolNode`
- Uses default error handler that only catches `ToolInvocationError`
- Any `ToolException` is re-raised and crashes `agent.invoke()`

**Default error handler** (`langchain/tools/tool_node.py`):
```python
def _default_handle_tool_errors(e: Exception) -> str:
    if isinstance(e, ToolInvocationError):
        return e.message  # ✅ Returns error to LLM
    raise e  # ❌ Re-raises everything else!
```

## Expected Behavior

Tools should be able to raise `ToolException` for recoverable errors (e.g., "File already exists", "Path not found", "Search string not found"), and the agent should:
1. Catch the exception
2. Convert it to a `ToolMessage` with the error details
3. Pass it to the LLM so it can retry with corrected parameters

This is the standard pattern documented for LangChain tools and works correctly when using `ToolNode(tools, handle_tool_errors=True)` directly.

## Proposed Solution

Add a `handle_tool_errors` parameter to `create_agent`:

```python
def create_agent(
    model: str | BaseChatModel,
    tools: Sequence[BaseTool | Callable | dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    *,
    handle_tool_errors: bool | str | Callable = True,  # ← New parameter
    # ... other parameters
) -> CompiledStateGraph:
    # ...

    # Pass error handling config to ToolNode
    tool_node = ToolNode(
        tools=available_tools,
        handle_tool_errors=handle_tool_errors  # ← Use parameter
    ) if available_tools else None
```

**Default to `True`** so all exceptions are caught by default, making tools more robust.

### System Info

> Python Version:  3.12.11
> langchain_core: 1.0.0a8
> langchain: 1.0.0a12

Title: [Feature Request] Token-aware Context Management and Compact Summaries
Creator: fehmisener
Body:
### Problem Description

Currently, Agno lacks native support for intelligent context window management based on token usage. Users face several limitations:

1. **No automatic history compaction**: When using `add_history_to_context=True`, the conversation history grows indefinitely until it hits model token limits, causing failures. [1](#6-0) 

2. **Fixed run count is inflexible**: The `num_history_runs` parameter requires specifying a fixed number of previous runs to include in context, which doesn't account for varying message lengths or token usage. [2](#6-1) 

3. **Summary generation timing**: `enable_session_summaries=True` generates summaries after every run, which is inefficient and unnecessary when the context is still within limits. [3](#6-2) 

4. **Manual workarounds required**: To implement token-aware history management, users must manually:
   - Retrieve the session
   - Check token metrics in `session_data["session_metrics"]` [4](#6-3) 
   - Clear `runs` array
   - Reset `session_metrics`
   - Generate summaries via `SessionSummaryManager`
   - Upsert the modified session back

This manual approach is error-prone and requires deep knowledge of Agno's internal session structure.

### Proposed Solution

Add native token-aware context management with the following features:

#### 1. Token-based History Compaction

```python
team = Team(
    members=[...],
    db=db,
    enable_token_aware_context=True,  # NEW
    max_context_tokens=8000,  # NEW: Token threshold for compaction
    context_compaction_strategy="summarize",  # NEW: "summarize" | "truncate" | "sliding_window"
    enable_session_summaries=True,
    add_session_summary_to_context=True,
)
```

#### 2. Automatic Summary Generation on Threshold

Instead of generating summaries after every run, only generate them when:
- Token threshold is reached
- Session is about to be compacted
- User explicitly requests via API

#### 3. Transparent Session Reset

When the token threshold is exceeded:
1. Automatically generate/update session summary
2. Clear `runs` array
3. Reset `session_metrics` to zero
4. Preserve `summary`, `team_data`, and `metadata`
5. Continue with fresh context + summary

#### 4. New Session Methods

```python
# Check if compaction is needed
team.should_compact_session(session_id="...")

# Manually trigger compaction
team.compact_session(session_id="...", preserve_summary=True)

# Get token usage for session
team.get_session_token_usage(session_id="...")
```

### Alternatives Considered

#### Alternative 1: Dynamic `num_history_runs`
Automatically adjust `num_history_runs` based on token count. However, this doesn't solve the summary generation inefficiency or provide clean session resets.

#### Alternative 2: Sliding Window with Token Limit
Keep only the most recent messages that fit within token limit. This loses older context entirely without summarization.

#### Alternative 3: External Token Management
Leave it to users to implement. This is the current state and creates friction for a common use case.

### Additional Context

#### Benefits

1. **Automatic context management**: No manual session manipulation required
2. **Efficient resource usage**: Summaries only generated when needed
3. **Predictable behavior**: Token limits prevent unexpected model failures
4. **Maintains continuity**: Session summaries preserve conversation context across compactions
5. **Flexible strategies**: Users can choose between summarization, truncation, or sliding windows

#### Implementation Notes

The implementation should:
- Integrate with existing `SessionSummaryManager` [5](#6-4) 
- Work with all database backends (PostgreSQL, Redis, Firestore, etc.)
- Support both `Agent` and `Team` classes
- Maintain backward compatibility with existing `num_history_runs` behavior
- Provide clear metrics/logging when compaction occurs

```python
def _adaptive_context_management(
    self, threshold_percentage: float = 0.60, runs_to_keep: int = 5
):
    """
    Adaptive context management for the Agno team.

    Args:
        threshold_percentage: Percentage of model context to trigger management (0.0 to 1.0)
        runs_to_keep: Number of recent runs to keep when summarizing
    """
    try:
        session = self._team.get_session(session_id=self.session_id)

        if not session:
            logger.debug(
                "AgnoSupervisor: No session found for adaptive context management"
            )
            return

        if not session.runs or len(session.runs) == 0:
            logger.debug(
                "AgnoSupervisor: Session has no runs for context management"
            )
            return

        # Get messages from all runs to check total context
        history_messages = session.get_messages_from_last_n_runs(
            skip_role="system",
            team_id=str(self.worker_config.id),
        )

        if not history_messages:
            logger.debug("AgnoSupervisor: No history messages found")
            return

        # Find the last assistant message with metrics (iterate from the end)
        last_assistant_message = history_messages[-1]
        if not (
            last_assistant_message.role == "assistant"
            and hasattr(last_assistant_message, "metrics")
            and last_assistant_message.metrics
        ):
            for message in reversed(history_messages):
                if (
                    message.role == "assistant"
                    and hasattr(message, "metrics")
                    and message.metrics
                ):
                    last_assistant_message = message
                    break

        if not last_assistant_message:
            logger.debug("AgnoSupervisor: No assistant message with metrics found")
            return

        # Get total tokens from the last message
        total_used_tokens = last_assistant_message.metrics.total_tokens

        # Get model ID and calculate threshold
        model_id = (
            self._team.model.id
            if self._team.model and hasattr(self._team.model, "id")
            else "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"
        )
        threshold_tokens, _ = calculate_context_threshold(
            model_id, threshold_percentage
        )

        if total_used_tokens > threshold_tokens:
            logger.debug(
                f"AgnoSupervisor: Triggering context management - "
                f"tokens: {total_used_tokens}/{threshold_tokens}, model: {model_id}, "
                f"threshold: {threshold_percentage * 100}%"
            )

            # Create a summary of the session
            try:
                system_prompt = dedent(
                    """\
                <summary-prompt-goes-here>
                """
                )

                session_summary_manager = SessionSummaryManager(
                    model=Gemini(id="gemini-2.5-flash"),
                    session_summary_prompt=system_prompt,
                )

                summary = session_summary_manager.create_session_summary(session)
                session.summary = summary

                total_runs = len(session.runs)

                if total_runs > runs_to_keep:
                    session.runs = session.runs[-runs_to_keep:]
                else:
                    session.runs = []

                self._team.save_session(session)

                logger.debug(
                    f"AgnoSupervisor: Successfully reduced context - "
                    f"removed {total_runs - runs_to_keep} runs, kept {len(session.runs)} runs, "
                    f"added summary with {len(summary) if summary else 0} characters"
                )

            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(
                    f"AgnoSupervisor: Failed to create session summary: {e}",
                    exc_info=True,
                )
                return

        else:
            logger.debug(
                f"AgnoSupervisor: Context within limits - "
                f"tokens: {total_used_tokens}/{threshold_tokens}, model: {model_id}, "
                f"threshold: {threshold_percentage * 100}%"
            )

    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(
            f"AgnoSupervisor: Error in adaptive context management: {e}",
            exc_info=True,
        )
```

That’s awesome, thanks a lot for the effort, team 🚀 

@dirkbrnd I’m wondering if we could also think about the `session.runs` column. As mentioned above, we manage context ourselves and effectively set `num_history_runs=999`. The problem is that `session.runs` stores previous runs *including all prior messages*, which creates a recursive tree. As a result, even relatively small conversations can grow to **hundreds of MBs** very quickly.

Limiting `num_history_runs` isn’t ideal for us because we lose earlier messages even when they’re just a few tokens.

One of our sessions recently hit ~200 MB in the `runs` column, and aside from the system message and first run, it was mostly human-to-agent conversation. This also starts breaking DB `upsert` operations.

Also mentioned in #5741

### Description

When a deepagent successfully delegates a task to a subagent using the task tool, the entire application crashes with a TypeError when the subagent completes its work and returns its result.

This error occurs specifically when the subagent's task does not involve file operations. The subagent executes its tools correctly (e.g., fetching data from an API) and generates a valid text-based report. However, the crash happens during the final step where the main agent tries to integrate the subagent's state back into its own.

### The core of the issue lies in how state is passed from a completed subagent back to the main agent.

1. Subagent State Return: When a subagent finishes, it returns its final state to the main agent. If the subagent performed no file operations, its internal files state channel appears to default to an empty list ([]).
2. Main Agent State Update: The main agent receives the subagent's output, which includes the key-value pair 'files': []. It then attempts to update its own files state with this value.
3. Reducer Failure: The state update is handled by the file_reducer function in deepagents/state.py. This function is defined as return {**l, **r}, which uses dictionary unpacking.
4. Type Error: The reducer receives the current files state (a dictionary, l) and the incoming update (the list [], r). The operation {**l, **[]} fails because the ** operator cannot be used on a list, raising the TypeError: 'list' object is not a mapping.

### How to reproduce
1. Create a deepagent with at least one subagent.
2. Assign the main agent a task that must be delegated to the subagent (e.g., "Use the azure_devops agent to fetch work items").
3. Ensure the subagent's delegated task involves API calls or data processing, but no file I/O.
4. The subagent will run and successfully generate a result.
5. Observe that the application crashes with the TypeError as the main agent attempts to process the final ToolMessage from the task. The nature of the task should be long running, involving multiple ToolCalls.

Additionaly, a potential fix that stopped the issue for me was : 
`def file_reducer(l, r):
    # Gracefully handle non-dicitionary updates from subagents
    if not isinstance(r, dict):
        return l
    if not isinstance(l, dict):
        l = {}
    return {**l, **r}`

```python
@staticmethod

                text=resp["output"]["text"],
                generation_info=dict(
                    finish_reason=resp["output"]["finish_reason"],
                    request_id=resp["request_id"],
```

Title: [Bug] Mounting AgentOS app on existing FastAPI prevents MCP tools connection
Creator: antipopp
Body:
### Description

Similarly as discussed in issue #4942 , when trying to run the app mounted on an existing FastAPI app, the MCP connection is not established.

The merged fix in #4949 doesn't apply to this use case.

This is needed so that we can run the AgentOS app in an existing server but on a different base path

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the server
2. Ask what tools are available

### Agent Configuration (if applicable)

```python
import uvicorn
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.openai import OpenAIChat
from agno.os import AgentOS
from agno.tools.mcp import MCPTools
from fastapi import FastAPI

mcp_tools = MCPTools(
    transport="streamable-http",
    url="https://docs.agno.com/mcp",
)

agent = Agent(
    name="Assistant",
    model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-5-mini"),
    instructions=["You are a helpful AI assistant."],
    markdown=True,
    tools=[mcp_tools],
)

# Custom FastAPI app
app: FastAPI = FastAPI(
    title="Custom FastAPI App",
    version="1.0.0",
)


# Setup our AgentOS app by passing your FastAPI app
agent_os = AgentOS(
    description="Example app with custom routers",
    agents=[agent],
)

agent_os_app = agent_os.get_app()

app.mount("/my-agent-os", agent_os_app)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(
        "my-app:app",
        host="0.0.0.0",
        port=7777,
        reload=True,
    )

```

### Expected Behavior

MCP connection should be established

### Actual Behavior

It doesn't connect to the MCP server

### Screenshots or Logs (if applicable)

_No response_

### Environment

```markdown
- Agno: 2.1.3
- Python: 3.12.11
```

### Possible Solutions (optional)

Comments:
[1] faizan842 (2025-10-09T09:29:14Z):
Hello @antipopp , I'm interested in working on this issue and contributing a fix. Please let me know if it's okay for me to proceed.

[2] manuhortet (2025-10-10T09:01:50Z):
Hey @antipopp

Your FastAPI app has its own lifecycle, which we can't control from the AgentOS instance.

For the MCP tools to be available in that lifecycle, you will need to handle the connection and closure of your `MCPTools` instance via FastAPI lifespans provided to your app. Like this:

```python
# Custom lifespan to handle MCP tools lifecycle as part of your app's lifecyle
@asynccontextmanager
async def custom_lifespan(_):
    # Startup: connect external MCP tools
    await mcp_tools.connect()

    yield

    # Shutdown: disconnect external MCP tools
    await mcp_tools.close()


# Custom FastAPI app
app: FastAPI = FastAPI(
    lifespan=custom_lifespan,
    ...
)
```

Let me know if this works for you. Happy to help further if not!

[3] antipopp (2025-10-10T12:23:32Z):
Ah! Thanks a lot, maybe it would be worth it specifying it in the docs under the "Bring you own app" section.

Creator: orinciog

### Problem Description

Hy!

* agent card discovery https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/topics/agent-discovery/ 

Thank you.

### Proposed Solution

Creating automatically an agent card with all its skills and tools and serving at a URL like `.well-known/agent-card.json` will be very helpful.

The nice think here is that you have all the necessary info for creating and serving this card (name, description, url, capabilities and skills).

[1] orinciog (2025-11-03T14:24:37Z):
@manuhortet 

We are using the following code for A2A agent cards. Its role is to derive automatically the agent card from all agno properties. 

```
from typing import Any
from uuid import uuid4
import json
from a2a.types import (
    AgentCard,
)
from agno.session import AgentSession
from agno.run.agent import RunOutput
from agno.os.utils import (
    format_tools,
)

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from agno.os import AgentOS


class AgnoAgentCard:
    """
    Connects to a remote A2A agent and provides a uniform method to delegate tasks
    """

    def __init__(self, agent,
                 version: str = "1.0.0",
                 additional_skills: list[dict[str, Any]] = None):
        self.agent = agent
        self.version = version
        self.additional_skills = additional_skills or []

    def create_agent_card(self) -> AgentCard:
        """
        Create AgentCard

        Returns:
            AgentCard: Card containing Agent information
        """
        # Get Agent information
        name = self.agent.name or "Unknown Agent"
        description = self.agent.description or self.agent.role or "An AI agent"

        # Get tool information (as skills)
        skills = list(self.additional_skills)
        if hasattr(self.agent, "get_tools"):
            # Use a temporary session ID to get tool list
            agent_tools = self.agent.get_tools(
                session=AgentSession(session_id=str(uuid4()), session_data={}),
                run_response=RunOutput(run_id=str(uuid4()))
            )
            formatted_tools = format_tools(
                agent_tools) if agent_tools else None
            if formatted_tools:
                for i, tool in enumerate(formatted_tools):
                    tool_name = tool.get("name", f"tool_{i}")
                    if tool.get("description"):
                        tool_description = tool["description"]
                    elif tool.get("parameters"):
                        tool_description = f"Tool: {json.dumps(tool['parameters'])}"
                    # Check if tool has a description attribute (Agno Function
                    # class)
                    elif hasattr(tool, "description") and tool.description:
                        tool_description = tool.description
                    elif hasattr(tool, "__doc__") and tool.__doc__:
                        tool_description = tool.__doc__.strip()
                    else:
                        tool_description = f"No description available for tool {tool_name}"

                    skills.append({
                        "id": f"tool_{i}_{tool_name}",
                        "name": tool_name,
                        "description": tool_description,
                        "tags": []
                    })

        # If no tools, add a default skill
        if not skills:
            skills.append({
                "id": "conversation",
                "name": "conversation",
                "description": "Able to conduct conversation.",
                "tags": []
            })

        # Create AgentCard
        return AgentCard(
            name=name,
            description=description,
            url="/a2a/message/send",
            version=self.version,
            defaultInputModes=["text"],
            defaultOutputModes=["text"],
            capabilities={
                # "streaming": self.agent.is_streamable,
                "streaming": False,
                "pushNotifications": False
            },
            skills=skills
        )

class AgentOSCard:
    """
    Connects to a remote A2A agent and provides a uniform method to delegate tasks
    """

    def __init__(self, agent_os: AgentOS):
        self.agent_os = agent_os
        self.agents = agent_os.agents or []
        self.teams = agent_os.teams or []

    def expose_cards(self, app: FastAPI):
        """
        Expose agent cards as a FastAPI application.
        """
        skill_dict = {}
        for agent in self.agents:
            if not agent.id:
                agent.set_id()
            card = AgnoAgentCard(agent)
            skill_dict[agent.id] = card.create_agent_card(
            ).model_dump(exclude_none=True)

        for team in self.teams:
            if not team.id:
                team.set_id()
            card = AgnoAgentCard(team)
            skill_dict[team.id] = card.create_agent_card(
            ).model_dump(exclude_none=True)

        # Add routes for agent cards
        for agent_id in skill_dict:
            route_path = f"/{agent_id}/.well-known/agent-card.json"

            def create_agent_card_handler(agent_id_inner=agent_id):
                async def agent_card():
                    return JSONResponse(
                        skill_dict.get(
                            agent_id_inner, {
                                "status": "unknown"}))
                return agent_card
            app.add_api_route(
                route_path,
                create_agent_card_handler(agent_id),
                methods=["GET"],
                tags=["A2A Discovery"])
```

and its usage is:
```

agent_os = AgentOS(
    id="my-first-os",
    description="My first AgentOS",
    agents=[assistant],
    teams=[team],
    a2a_interface=True,
)

app = agent_os.get_app()

#New lines added to expose A2A cards
agent_osa2a=AgentOSCard(agent_os=agent_os)
agent_osa2a.expose_cards(app)
#End of exposing A2A cards
```

My question is do you plan to support this feature? If I submit a PR, is aligned with your ideas regarding the future of A2A in agno? 

Thank you.

- Should this be on by default or behind a flag?
- For unknown models, skip validation or show a generic warning?

Let me know if this looks good @mdrxy , also it should be non-breaking imo.

[3] mdrxy (2025-10-10T19:31:56Z):
@raunaqness @ArjunJagdale I wrote down this idea so that it wouldn't be forgotten ;) it's not necessarily guaranteed yet, more just exploratory at this point.

I think we should consider the architecture at a high level before starting implementation.

Presumably this pattern should work for all chat model integrations supported by LangChain. 

I'm not sure whether it makes sense to maintain, for instance, a `.yaml` file for each model provider package, or to centralize things somewhere in `langchain-core`

> For unknown models, skip validation or show a generic warning?

@ArjunJagdale if we don't know the model, we don't have an entries in our "capabilities table" to check against. It is unlikely that we would be able to maintain a canonical list of all capabilities provided by all models. So, I think it is reasonable to **not warn** in such case and let the error surface during execution.

> Should this be on by default or behind a flag?

I think it's reasonable to enable this by default, but would need to consider it in more depth. We could introduce a flag to bypass validation.

### Description

Using the provided JWT middleware (or any middleware that passes a `request.state.dependencies` dictionary) the agent has no access to those infos. I've also tried to add the `add_dependencies_to_context` prop but the result it still the same.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the [JWT Middleware with Authorization Headers](https://docs.agno.com/examples/agent-os/middleware/jwt-middleware) example
2. ```bash 
     curl --location 'http://localhost:7777/agents/user-agent/runs' \
    --header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
    --header 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
    --data-urlencode 'message=What do you know about me?'```

### Agent Configuration (if applicable)

```python
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta

import jwt
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.openai import OpenAIChat
from agno.os import AgentOS
from agno.os.middleware import JWTMiddleware

# JWT Secret (use environment variable in production)
JWT_SECRET = "a-string-secret-at-least-256-bits-long"


# Define a tool that uses dependencies claims
def get_user_details(dependencies: dict):
    """
    Get the current user's details.
    """
    return {
        "name": dependencies.get("name"),
        "email": dependencies.get("email"),
        "roles": dependencies.get("roles"),
    }


# Create agent
research_agent = Agent(
    id="user-agent",
    model=OpenAIChat(id="gpt-5-mini"),
    tools=[get_user_details],
    instructions="You are a user agent that can get user details if the user asks for them.",
    add_dependencies_to_context=True,  # Add dependencies claims to context
)


agent_os = AgentOS(
    description="JWT Protected AgentOS",
    agents=[research_agent],
)

# Get the final app
app = agent_os.get_app()

# Add JWT middleware to the app
# This middleware will automatically inject JWT values into request.state and is used in the relevant endpoints.
app.add_middleware(
    JWTMiddleware,
    secret_key=JWT_SECRET,  # or use JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable
    algorithm="HS256",
    user_id_claim="sub",  # Extract user_id from 'sub' claim
    session_id_claim="session_id",  # Extract session_id from 'session_id' claim
    dependencies_claims=["name", "email", "roles"],
    # In this example, we want this middleware to demonstrate parameter injection, not token validation.
    # In production scenarios, you will probably also want token validation. Be careful setting this to False.
    validate=False,
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    """
    Run your AgentOS with JWT parameter injection.

    Test by calling /agents/user-agent/runs with a message: "What do you know about me?"
    """
    # Test token with user_id and session_id:
    payload = {
        "sub": "user_123",  # This will be injected as user_id parameter
        "session_id": "demo_session_456",  # This will be injected as session_id parameter
        "exp": datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(hours=24),
        "iat": datetime.now(UTC),
        # Dependency claims
        "name": "John Doe",
        "email": "john.doe@example.com",
        "roles": ["admin", "user"],
    }
    token = jwt.encode(payload, JWT_SECRET, algorithm="HS256")
    print("Test token:")
    print(token)
    agent_os.serve(app="test_jwt:app", port=7777, reload=True)
```

The agent should have those infos

Title: [Feature Request] Workflow in a Workflow
Creator: JerYme
Body:
### Problem Description

Hello, starting to build multiple complex workflows, I am looking for the best way to compose, orchestrate all these workflows together, as some kind of a graph.

I would like to know if there is a way to use Workflows as Steps.

From the documentation : 

> Workflows excel at deterministic agent automation, while [Teams] are designed for dynamic agentic coordination. 
Workflows execute as a controlled sequence of steps, where each step produces deterministic outputs that feed into the next step. 

> Step Types
Agents: Individual AI executors with specific capabilities and instructions
Teams: Coordinated groups of agents working together on complex problems
Functions: Custom Python functions for specialized processing logic

In Step Types, we don't have Workflows available, I could wraps them up in Step or Functions , Teams are included, why not include Workflows ?

It's more an open question than a regular Feature Request.
Thank you

### Proposed Solution

Support Workflows as Step Types, same as Teams.

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Additional Context

_No response_

### Would you like to work on this?

- [ ] Yes, I’d love to work on it!
- [ ] I’m open to collaborating but need guidance.
- [x] No, I’m just sharing the idea.

### Description

After upgrading Agno from v1.8.2 to v2.1.4, I encountered an unexpected ⁠TypeError when calling ⁠agent.continue_run with ⁠run_id, as suggested in the [documentation](https://docs.agno.com/concepts/hitl/overview#dynamic-user-input).

```
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.openrouter import OpenRouter
from agno.tools.toolkit import Toolkit
from agno.tools.user_control_flow import UserControlFlowTools
from agno.utils import pprint


# Example toolkit for handling emails
class EmailTools(Toolkit):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(
            name="EmailTools", tools=[self.send_email, self.get_emails], *args, **kwargs
        )

    def send_email(self, subject: str, body: str, to_address: str) -> str:
        """Send an email to the given address with the given subject and body.

        Args:
            subject (str): The subject of the email.
            body (str): The body of the email.
            to_address (str): The address to send the email to.
        """
        return f"Sent email to {to_address} with subject {subject} and body {body}"

    def get_emails(self, date_from: str, date_to: str) -> str:
        """Get all emails between the given dates.

        Args:
            date_from (str): The start date.
            date_to (str): The end date.
        """
        return [
            {
                "subject": "Hello",
                "body": "Hello, world!",
                "to_address": "test@test.com",
                "date": date_from,
            },
            {
                "subject": "Random other email",
                "body": "This is a random other email",
                "to_address": "john@doe.com",
                "date": date_to,
            },
        ]


agent = Agent(
    model=OpenRouter(id="google/gemini-2.5-flash"),
    tools=[EmailTools(), UserControlFlowTools()],
    markdown=True,
    debug_mode=True,
```

Title: Add observational hooks (before_tool/after_tool) for tool calls in AgentMiddleware
Creator: HY-love-sleep
Body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a feature request, not a bug report or usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes the feature request.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar feature request and didn't find it.
- [x] I checked the LangChain documentation and API reference to see if this feature already exists.
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.

### Feature Description

Currently, AgentMiddleware in langchain_v1 provides asymmetric hooks for model and tool calls:
Model hooks (3 types):
✅ before_model - Observational hook
✅ after_model - Observational hook
✅ wrap_model_call - Interceptor hook
Tool hooks (only 1 type):
❌ No before_tool hook
❌ No after_tool hook
✅ wrap_tool_call - Interceptor hook only
Request: Add before_tool and after_tool observational hooks to AgentMiddleware to provide symmetric API design and enable simple, declarative tool call monitoring without requiring the interceptor pattern.

### Use Case

Problem:
When building agent applications, I need to:
Log tool call inputs/outputs for debugging and auditing
Track tool execution metrics (latency, success rate, etc.)
Monitor tool usage patterns across different tools
Implement simple pre/post processing without controlling execution flow
Current Workaround:
I have to use wrap_tool_call even for simple observational tasks

### Proposed Solution

_No response_

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Additional Context

_No response_
Comments:
[1] eyurtsev (2025-10-11T13:51:40Z):
Use the tool interceptor or before_model call for this. If that doesn't work would love a good explanation for why not. We're only going to add hooks that enable new capabilities rather than hooks that provide a 2nd way to do the same thing.

[2] HY-love-sleep (2025-10-13T02:26:09Z):
> Use the tool interceptor or before_model call for this. If that doesn't work would love a good explanation for why not. We're only going to add hooks that enable new capabilities rather than hooks that provide a 2nd way to do the same thing.

Currently I can use the wrap_tool_call record tool to enter/out parameters and read them in the next round of before_model, which really does the job. But my reasons for why need two extra hooks are as follows：

Semantic asymmetry: model has before/after + wrap; tool only wraps, API asymmetry, and higher cost to learn/use mind.
Mixed responsibilities: For "pure observation", it is also necessary to use an interceptor with a "controllable process", which has more coupling capacity than is required and is easy to mix with real control logic (retry, short circuit).
Composability/readability: observational hooks can be combined sequentially, and the code is more intuitive; The wrap chain is used to control the flow, and the separation of duties between the two is clearer.
Clear timing: Provides before_tool/after_tool accurate observation at the same round and node, rather than indirect observation in the "next round before_model".

[3] eyurtsev (2025-10-17T15:53:08Z):
The correct way to handle the use cases is through the wrap_tool_call interceptor.

We can re-consider if there are more convincing use cases that cannot be solved with the existing hooks.

[4] eyurtsev (2025-10-20T15:40:51Z):
Closing this issue for now as not work is planned for it. We'd want something motivated by actual use cases

Title: [Feature Request] Improve DashScope structured outputs and regional endpoint selection
Creator: Vist233
Body:
### Problem Description

When the DashScope model (libs/agno/agno/models/dashscope/dashscope.py) is used with Agent(..., output_schema=...), the SDK upgrades the request to response_format={"type": "json_object"} (or JSON Schema). DashScope rejects that request with HTTP 400 unless at least one message literally contains “json”, so callers without that hint see <400> InternalError.Algo.InvalidParameter: 'messages' must contain the word 'json'…. At the same time, teams operating in mainland China need a seamless way to hit the domestic DashScope endpoint instead of the default Singapore one—today they must override base_url manually.

### Proposed Solution

Align the core package with the branch changes already tested in libs/agno/agno/models/dashscope/dashscope.py:
• __post_init__ now derives the correct base URL from a new region argument, automatically routing "CN"/"China" variants to https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 while keeping other regions on the international endpoint.
• _ensure_json_hint inspects outgoing messages; when the response format is JSON and no message mentions “json”, it prepends a system reminder "Please return in JSON format".。 so DashScope accepts structured output.
• All synchronous and asynchronous invocation paths (invoke, ainvoke, invoke_stream, ainvoke_stream) call _ensure_json_hint before delegating to the base implementation, ensuring the hint is applied uniformly.
The current branch implementation is available for review at https://github.com/Vist233/agno/commit/9d4283e319c8db5d812249d3752e69c5822f25c8.

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Additional Context

Cookbook samples don’t fail because their prompts already mention “JSON”; the issue targets natural prompts that omit it. Goal is to have both structured output autofix and regional endpoint handling covered together.

Title: `ModelResponse` cannot be imported from `langchain.agents.middleware` despite being defined in `types.py` and documented in official docs (v1.0.0a14)
Creator: bart0401
Body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I read what a minimal reproducible example is (https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example).
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Example Code

## Example Code

### ❌ **Code that FAILS** (as documented in official docs)

```python
# This import statement is shown in the official documentation:
# https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware#wrap-style-hooks
from langchain.agents.middleware import AgentMiddleware, ModelRequest, ModelResponse

# Result: ImportError
```

### ✅ **Code that WORKS** (workaround)

```python
# Direct import from types.py works fine
from langchain.agents.middleware import AgentMiddleware, ModelRequest
from langchain.agents.middleware.types import ModelResponse

# This works!
print(ModelResponse)
# Output: <class 'langchain.agents.middleware.types.ModelResponse'>
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```python
from langchain.agents.middleware import ModelResponse
```

**Output:**
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
ImportError: cannot import name 'ModelResponse' from 'langchain.agents.middleware'
(/path/to/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langchain/agents/middleware/__init__.py)
```

### Description

### What I'm trying to do:
I'm implementing a retry middleware for model calls using LangChain's middleware system, following the official documentation at [https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware#wrap-style-hooks](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langchain/middleware#wrap-style-hooks).

### What I expect to happen:
According to the official documentation, I should be able to import `ModelResponse` directly from `langchain.agents.middleware`:

```python
from langchain.agents.middleware import AgentMiddleware, ModelRequest, ModelResponse
```

### What is currently happening:
The import fails with an `ImportError` stating that `ModelResponse` cannot be imported from `langchain.agents.middleware`.

---

## Root Cause Analysis

After investigating the source code, I found that:

### 1. **`ModelResponse` IS defined** in `types.py`:

**File:** `langchain/agents/middleware/types.py` (lines 80-93)
```python
@dataclass
class ModelResponse:
    """Response from model execution including messages and optional structured output.

    The result will usually contain a single AIMessage, but may include
    an additional ToolMessage if the model used a tool for structured output.
    """

    result: list[BaseMessage]
    """List of messages from model execution."""

    structured_response: Any = None
    """Parsed structured output if response_format was specified, None otherwise."""
```

### 2. **`ModelResponse` IS exported in `types.py.__all__`:**

**File:** `langchain/agents/middleware/types.py` (lines 42-57)
```python
__all__ = [
    "AgentMiddleware",
    "AgentState",
    "ContextT",
    "ModelRequest",
    "ModelResponse",  # ✅ Present here!
    "OmitFromSchema",
    "PublicAgentState",
    "after_agent",
    "after_model",
    "before_agent",
    "before_model",
    "dynamic_prompt",
    "hook_config",
    "wrap_tool_call",
]
```

### 3. **`ModelResponse` is NOT imported in `__init__.py`:**

**File:** `langchain/agents/middleware/__init__.py` (lines 20-31)
```python
from .types import (
    AgentMiddleware,
    AgentState,
    ModelRequest,      # ✅ Imported
    # ModelResponse,   # ❌ MISSING!
    after_agent,
    after_model,
    before_agent,
    before_model,
    dynamic_prompt,
    hook_config,
    wrap_model_call,
)
```

### 4. **`ModelResponse` is NOT in `__init__.py.__all__`:**

**File:** `langchain/agents/middleware/__init__.py` (lines 33-59)
```python
__all__ = [
    "AgentMiddleware",
    "AgentState",
    # should move to langchain-anthropic if we decide to keep it
    "AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware",
    "ClearToolUsesEdit",
    "ContextEditingMiddleware",
    "HumanInTheLoopMiddleware",
    "InterruptOnConfig",
    "LLMToolEmulator",
    "LLMToolSelectorMiddleware",
    "ModelCallLimitMiddleware",
    "ModelFallbackMiddleware",
    "ModelRequest",    # ✅ Present
    # "ModelResponse", # ❌ MISSING!
    "PIIDetectionError",
    "PIIMiddleware",
    "PlanningMiddleware",
    "SummarizationMiddleware",
    "ToolCallLimitMiddleware",
    "after_agent",
    "after_model",
    "before_agent",
    "before_model",
    "dynamic_prompt",
    "hook_config",
    "wrap_model_call",
]
```

---

## Suggested Fix

Add `ModelResponse` to both the import statement and `__all__` list in `langchain/agents/middleware/__init__.py`:

```python
from .types import (
    AgentMiddleware,
    AgentState,
    ModelRequest,
    ModelResponse,  # ← Add this line
    after_agent,
    after_model,
    before_agent,
    before_model,
    dynamic_prompt,
    hook_config,
    wrap_model_call,
)

__all__ = [
    "AgentMiddleware",
    "AgentState",
    # ... other exports ...
    "ModelRequest",
    "ModelResponse",  # ← Add this line
    # ... other exports ...
]
```

```markdown
agno: 2.1.4
pymysql: 1.1.2
```

Fix `get_knowledge_contents` function in MySQLDb.

In Knowledge class:
- `get_content` calls `get_knowledge_contents` from `BaseDb`, in this case I am using `MySQLDb`.

Title: AgentMiddleware lacks async support - NotImplementedError in awrap_model_call for some built-in middleware (1.0.0a14)
Creator: bart0401
Body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title that summarizes this issue.
- [x] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [x] I am sure that this is a bug in LangChain rather than my code.
- [x] The bug is not resolved by updating to the latest stable version of LangChain (or the specific integration package).
- [x] This is not related to the langchain-community package.
- [x] I read what a minimal reproducible example is (https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example).
- [x] I posted a self-contained, minimal, reproducible example. A maintainer can copy it and run it AS IS.

### Example Code

```python
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import PlanningMiddleware
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic

# Create agent with middleware
model = ChatAnthropic(model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022")
agent = create_agent(
    model=model,
    system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant",
    tools=[],
    middleware=[PlanningMiddleware()],
)

# Try to invoke asynchronously
config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "test"}}
await agent.ainvoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}, config)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```
NotImplementedError: Asynchronous implementation of awrap_model_call is not available.
You are likely encountering this error because you defined only the sync version (wrap_model_call)
and invoked your agent in an asynchronous context (e.g., using `astream()` or `ainvoke()`).
To resolve this, either:
(1) subclass AgentMiddleware and implement the asynchronous awrap_model_call method,
(2) use the @wrap_model_call decorator on a standalone async function, or
(3) invoke your agent synchronously using `stream()` or `invoke()`.
```

### Description

### Problem Summary

Several built-in middleware classes in **LangChain 1.0.0a14** do not implement `awrap_model_call()`, which causes `NotImplementedError` when agents are invoked asynchronously using methods like `ainvoke()`, `astream()`, or `astream_events()`.

### Affected Middleware

**❌ Async NOT Supported** (NotImplementedError):
- `PlanningMiddleware`
- `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware`
- `ModelFallbackMiddleware`

**✅ Async Supported** (Working correctly):
- `PIIMiddleware`
- `SummarizationMiddleware`
- `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware`

**Note**: Any custom middleware inheriting from `AgentMiddleware` without implementing `awrap_model_call()` will also fail in async contexts.

### Root Cause Analysis

All middleware classes inherit the `awrap_model_call()` method from the base `AgentMiddleware` class, which only raises `NotImplementedError`:

```python
# From langchain.agents.middleware.types.AgentMiddleware
async def awrap_model_call(
    self,
    request: ModelRequest,
    handler: Callable[[ModelRequest], Awaitable[ModelResponse]],
) -> ModelCallResult:
    msg = (
        "Asynchronous implementation of awrap_model_call is not available. "
        "You are likely encountering this error because you defined only the sync version "
        "(wrap_model_call) and invoked your agent in an asynchronous context..."
    )
    raise NotImplementedError(msg)
```

**Some middleware classes** (`PlanningMiddleware`, `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware`, `ModelFallbackMiddleware`) do not override this method, while others (`PIIMiddleware`, `SummarizationMiddleware`, `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware`) have properly implemented async support.

### Verification Steps

We've tested all built-in middleware with actual async agent invocations:

```python
import asyncio
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import PlanningMiddleware
from langchain_anthropic import ChatAnthropic

async def test_middleware():
    model = ChatAnthropic(model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022")

    # Test PlanningMiddleware (will fail)
    agent = create_agent(
        model=model,
        system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant",
        tools=[],
        middleware=[PlanningMiddleware()],
    )

    config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": "test"}}
    # This will raise NotImplementedError
    await agent.ainvoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}, config)

asyncio.run(test_middleware())
```

**Test Results:**

- ✅ `PIIMiddleware`: Works with async
- ✅ `SummarizationMiddleware`: Works with async
- ✅ `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware`: Works with async
- ❌ `PlanningMiddleware`: NotImplementedError
- ❌ `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware`: NotImplementedError
- ❌ `ModelFallbackMiddleware`: NotImplementedError

### Impact on Real-World Use Cases

This issue affects all modern async Python applications:
- ✅ **WebSocket streaming**: Real-time agent responses in chat applications
- ✅ **SSE (Server-Sent Events)**: Server-side streaming for progressive responses
- ✅ **FastAPI async endpoints**: Modern async web frameworks (FastAPI, Starlette)
- ✅ **DeepAgents**: Async multi-agent orchestration patterns
- ✅ **LangGraph async workflows**: State machine execution with async tools

### Expected Behavior

Middleware should work seamlessly in both sync and async contexts:

```python
# Both should work:
result = agent.invoke({"messages": [...]}, config)        # Sync ✅
result = await agent.ainvoke({"messages": [...]}, config) # Async ❌ (currently broken)
```

### Actual Behavior

Using the three affected middleware classes (`PlanningMiddleware`, `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware`, `ModelFallbackMiddleware`) with async agent methods raises `NotImplementedError`, forcing developers to:

1. Abandon those specific middleware entirely, or
2. Downgrade to synchronous agent execution (losing async benefits)

### Current Workaround

We've temporarily disabled the problematic middleware in our production environment:

```python
# Temporary workaround: Comment out unsupported middleware
agent = create_agent(
    model=model,
    system_prompt="You are a helpful assistant",
    tools=[],
    middleware=[
        # PlanningMiddleware(),  # ❌ Disabled - async not supported
        # AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware(),  # ❌ Disabled - async not supported
        PIIMiddleware(pii_type="email"),  # ✅ Works with async
        SummarizationMiddleware(model=model),  # ✅ Works with async
    ],
)
```

We've preserved the original middleware configuration in code comments for easy re-enablement once this issue is resolved.

### Suggested Fix

Implement `awrap_model_call()` for the three affected middleware classes (`PlanningMiddleware`, `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware`, `ModelFallbackMiddleware`). Here's a conceptual example:

```python
class PlanningMiddleware(AgentMiddleware):
    def wrap_model_call(
        self,
        request: ModelRequest,
        handler: Callable[[ModelRequest], ModelResponse],
    ) -> ModelCallResult:
        # Existing sync implementation
        ...

    async def awrap_model_call(
        self,
        request: ModelRequest,
        handler: Callable[[ModelRequest], Awaitable[ModelResponse]],
    ) -> ModelCallResult:
        # Async implementation with similar logic
        # Replace sync operations with async equivalents
        response = await handler(request)
        # ... rest of async logic
        return ModelCallResult(response=response)
```

### Additional Context

- This worked correctly in earlier LangChain versions with synchronous agent execution
- The issue emerged with the async-first agent APIs introduced in the 1.0.0 alpha series
- Our production stack: **FastAPI + LangGraph + DeepAgents** with WebSocket/SSE streaming
- We're running `deepagents` which uses `async_create_deep_agent(..., is_async=True)`
- We've verified through comprehensive testing that 3 out of 6 built-in middleware lack async support
- Good news: `PIIMiddleware`, `SummarizationMiddleware`, and `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware` already work correctly with async!
